clue.text: 17 cottage, bolted inside

definitions.note: 17 refers to the answer at 24/17, STONE

indicators.note: something kept inside is enclosed, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a gîte is a French holiday cottage
bolted means ran off

explanation.surface: A stone cottage has been locked up, with the doors bolted from inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 17 points to the second word of 24/17, so the definition is just 'stone'. 'Bolted' looks like locked, but it means fled.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock, a common building stone.

clue.text: Perhaps compound time in musical

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: Rent is a Broadway rock musical

explanation.surface: Perhaps a musical needs compound time signatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound time' looks like a musical term, but 'Perhaps compound' is the definition and 'time' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in a chemical reaction, and a compound is one example.

clue.text: Wound, having cut head — in need of dressing?

indicators.note: cutting the head off a word removes its opening letter

parts.note: wound as in twisted, past tense of wind

explanation.surface: A head wound that needs a dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' reads as an injury, which suits 'dressing', but it is the past tense of wind; dressing then means putting clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unclothed needs to get dressed, a playful reading of needing a dressing.

clue.text: A flower in dark colour for spring child

indicators.note: being in something means being enclosed by it

parts.note: tan is a brownish colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child picks a dark-coloured flower in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crossword code for a river, here the Ure in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under Taurus, late April to May, has a birthday in spring.

clue.text: Charge everyone minimal amount, saving millions

indicators.note: saving here means keeping hold of, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: 1p, one penny, is the smallest sum, read as IP
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
each one, everyone individually

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'everyone minimal amount' as 1p each; one penny is written 1P, taken as IP.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach is to formally accuse an official of misconduct, so it is to charge them.

clue.text: Little game turned on

indicators.note: something turned over is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
on in the sense of about, concerning

explanation.surface: A short game that was turned on.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty, small in quantity, so it is an adjective for little.

clue.text: Trump or Putin very soon confined to prison? On the contrary

something confined to a place is shut up within it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
in a mo, short for in a moment

explanation.surface: Will Trump or Putin soon be locked up? Or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' applies to the whole construction: the cage-with-insert is reversed in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is obsessed with themselves; the setter offers the two leaders as examples, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Sinner opening House of God

parts.note: a con, convict, is a wrongdoer
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A sinner opens the door of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is a religious house of nuns, a community devoted to God.

clue.text: Modern attribute of generous chap encapsulating sugar daddy?

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as if in a capsule, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: a soft heart is the mark of a kind, generous man
Henry Tate founded the sugar firm Tate & Lyle

explanation.surface: A generous man showing the trait of a sugar daddy.
explanation.walkthrough: A sugar daddy usually lavishes gifts on a young partner; here it is the father of a sugar business, Tate of Tate & Lyle, British sugar refiners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is the latest and most advanced in its field is modern.

clue.text: See 16
Where 26 12 goes? Not entirely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Cleopatra's Needle is an obelisk, which rises to a tip
second meaning: partly, to some extent

explanation.walkthrough: 26 12 is the London obelisk named in 26/12; an obelisk tapers to a pyramid-shaped tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partially, with limits, and literally describes rising all the way to a tip.

clue.text: See 26
Two figures, the first of which shortly punched by a bully

indicators.note: something punched has a hole made in it, so a piece is driven inside
shortly means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: two numbers, three and ten
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people, one of them briefly beaten up by a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first of the two numbers loses its last letter, and the A is driven in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, which is to threaten them.

clue.text: Scottish author set off with no idea, might you say?

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so these letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A Scottish author set off on a journey with no idea where he was going.
explanation.walkthrough: The old joke: what do you call a deer with no eyes? No idea. Venison, deer meat, minus its I gives the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped, was born in Edinburgh.

clue.text: Temperature ultimately ignored, I load ovens carelessly — burning food?

indicators.note: done carelessly, the letters are thrown together in a new order
a letter that is ignored is left out
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is taken

parts.note: ultimately points to the final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ignoring the temperature, I load the ovens carelessly and burn the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning' is the definition's joke: the food burns the mouth, not in the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindaloo is a very hot curry, so it is food that burns with spice.

clue.text: Written sign, black-skinned cat alongside it

indicators.note: a skin wraps round its contents, so one piece forms an outer layer for the rest

indicators.note: alongside means placed next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A written sign about a black-skinned cat beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black-skinned' means the dark word forms the skin around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditto mark is the pair of commas written to mean the same as above.

clue.text: See 24
Swelled, one pulled from drain, exhausted

parts.note: to tire is to drain of energy

bled as in drained dry

explanation.definitionFit: To treble is to triple in size, so trebled means grew or swelled threefold.

clue.text: Race in the sprawling metropolis

indicators.note: something sprawling spreads untidily, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: taken as written
a metropolis is a big city

explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a running event, but it means ethnic group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnicity is a person's ethnic group or descent, the sense in which race is used.

clue.text: Island city where someone spotting thief called out?

explanation.walkthrough: Nicker is British slang for a thief, from nick, to steal. The match in sound is approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital of Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Snippet of relevant info I located, covering sheet

indicators.note: a snippet is a small piece cut from a longer whole

parts.note: a run of letters inside these words
the run continues into this word's opening letter

explanation.surface: I found a scrap of useful information under a cover sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is thin metal sheeting used to wrap and cover food.

clue.text: Conventional cricketer ninety short of century, say?

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
Joe Root, the England batsman

explanation.surface: A conventional cricketer gets out ninety short of a century.
explanation.walkthrough: A century is 100; ninety short of that is 10, which is the square root of 100. Joe Root is an England batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten multiplied by itself makes a hundred, so it is the square root of a century; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Centre of Poitiers bypassed by beloved oldie in diversion through France?

one is a number

clue.text: Film of repairman dropping trousers — might this be?

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

clue.text: Massive erection, might that have mummy in stitches!?

definitions.text: might that have mummy in stitches!?
definitions.meaning: setter's reading: a huge erected monument whose name pairs an Egyptian queen, now a mummy, with a sewing tool

explanation.walkthrough: 'Erection' is a structure put up, 'mummy' is an embalmed Egyptian, and 'in stitches' hints at a sewing implement. The obelisk stands on the Thames Embankment in London.
